description:
Prove at the lease sequence that an interruption at any step leaves the lease file at its prior or its next value and never needs the claims log to recover.

## Background

Every lease change in `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs` runs under one held lease lock through one `apply` step: evict an expired lease, apply a pure change, publish the lease file by synced temp file and rename (or unlink) with a directory sync, bump `claims.seq`, append the operation's history lines to `claims.jsonl` in one write. The rename or unlink is the commit point. An acquire over an expired lease writes two history lines, the eviction and the acquire. No lease-level interruption seam exists: `MutationInterruptionInjector` (`storage/mutation_interruption.rs:13-33`) and `RedoInterruptionInjector` (`storage/redo_apply.rs:33-59`) cover repository sessions and redo records only.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A test-only interruption seam, shaped like `RedoInterruptionInjector`, can stop `apply` after each step.
- [hard] REQ-02: One matrix test interrupts acquire, renew, heartbeat, release and force-evict at every step and shows that the lease file then holds the prior or the next lease, that the next operation succeeds, and that the history log lacks at most the interrupted operation's history lines.
- [hard] REQ-03: A retried acquire after an interruption past the commit point finds its own lease and writes no duplicate.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: An interrupted lease operation leaves the prior or the next lease
